46421-coyotes-in-their-economic-relation.title: Coyotes In Their Economic Relations
46421-coyotes-in-their-economic-relation.creator: Unknown
46421-coyotes-in-their-economic-relation.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Intermediate in size between the foxes and the larger wolves, yet varying greatly in this respect with the different species, the coyotes are outwardly characterized by a sharp-pointed muzzle, upright ears, and a moderately long, bushy tail. The pelage is full, especially in winter.

arxiv-2102-13365.title: On the regularity theory for mixed local and nonlocal quasilinear elliptic equations
arxiv-2102-13365.creator: Prashanta Garain, Juha Kinnunen
arxiv-2102-13365.description: Abstract We consider a combination of local and nonlocal p p -Laplace equations and discuss several regularity properties of weak solutions. More precisely, we establish local boundedness of weak subsolutions, local Hölder continuity of weak solutions, Harnack inequality for weak solutions and weak Harnack inequality for weak supersolutions.

arxiv-2201-05807.title: Orbital Hall effect in crystals: inter-atomic versus intra-atomic contributions
arxiv-2201-05807.creator: Armando Pezo, Diego García Ovalle, Aurélien Manchon
arxiv-2201-05807.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Armando Pezo, Diego García Ovalle, Aurélien Manchon. The orbital Hall effect (OHE) designates the generation of a charge-neutral flow of orbital angular momentum transverse to an initial charge current. Recent theoretical investigations suggest that transition metals display sizable OHE, encouraging experimental search along this direction. Nonetheless, most of these theories assume that the orbital moment originates from the region immediately surrounding the atom core, adopting the so-called atomic center approximation .

arxiv-2201-09058.title: DeepScalper: A Risk-Aware Reinforcement Learning Framework to Capture Fleeting Intraday Trading Opportunities
arxiv-2201-09058.creator: Shuo Sun, Wanqi Xue, Rundong Wang, Xu He, Junlei Zhu, Jian Li, Bo An
arxiv-2201-09058.description: Abstract . Reinforcement learning (RL) techniques have shown great success in many challenging quantitative trading tasks, such as portfolio management and algorithmic trading. Especially, intraday trading is one of the most profitable and risky tasks because of the intraday behaviors of the financial market that reflect billions of rapidly fluctuating capitals.

arxiv-2204-11326.title: Beyond the Quadratic Approximation: the Multiscale Structure of Neural Network Loss Landscapes
arxiv-2204-11326.creator: Chao Ma, Daniel Kunin, Lei Wu, Lexing Ying
arxiv-2204-11326.description: Abstract A quadratic approximation of neural network loss landscapes has been extensively used to study the optimization process of these networks. Though, it usually holds in a very small neighborhood of the minimum, it cannot explain many phenomena observed during the optimization process.

arxiv-2205-05638.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
arxiv-2205-05638.creator: Haokun Liu, Derek Tam, Mohammed MuqeethJay MohtaTenghao HuangMohit BansalColin Raffel Department of Computer ScienceUniversity of North Carolina at Chapel Hill {haokunl,dtredsox,muqeeth,craffel}@cs.unc.edu
arxiv-2205-05638.description: Abstract Few-shot in-context learning (ICL) enables pre-trained language models to perform a previously-unseen task without any gradient-based training by feeding a small number of training examples as part of the input. ICL incurs substantial computational, memory, and storage costs because it involves processing all of the training examples every time a prediction is made. arxiv-2304-00255.creator: Marilena Crupi, Antonino Ficarra, Ernesto Lax
arxiv-2304-00255.description: Abstract . Let G G be a finite simple graph and let I ⁡ ( G ) I(G) be its edge ideal. In this article, we investigate the squarefree powers of I ⁡ ( G ) I(G) by means of Betti splittings.

arxiv-2401-17569.title: A high contrast and resolution reconstruction algorithm in quantitative photoacoustic tomography Thanks: Partially supported by the BMBF-Project iDeLIVER : Intelligent MR Diagnosis of the Liver by Linking Model and Data-driven Processes, US National Science Foundation Grant No: 2309491, and Universi
arxiv-2401-17569.creator: Anwesa Dey, Alfio Borzì, Souvik Roy
arxiv-2401-17569.description: Abstract A framework for reconstruction of optical diffusion and absorption coefficients in quantitative photoacoustic tomography is presented. This framework is based on a Tikhonov-type functional with a regularization term promoting sparsity of the absorption coefficient and a prior involving a Kubelka-Munk absorption-diffusion relation that allows to obtain superior reconstructions.

arxiv-2404-16916.title: Automating physical intuition in nonlinear fiber optics with unsupervised dominant balance search
arxiv-2404-16916.creator: Andrei V. Ermolaev, Christophe Finot, Goëry Genty, John M. Dudley
arxiv-2404-16916.description: Abstract Identifying the underlying processes that locally dominate physical interactions is the key to understanding nonlinear dynamics. Machine-learning techniques have recently been shown to be highly promising in automating the search for dominant physics, adding important insights that complement analytical methods and empirical intuition.

arxiv-2505-18644.title: Enhancing Generalization of Speech Large Language Models with Multi-Task Behavior Imitation and Speech-Text Interleaving
arxiv-2505-18644.creator: Jingran, Xiang, Hui, Yue, Yang, Xixin, Zhiyong
arxiv-2505-18644.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable generalization across tasks, leading to increased interest in integrating speech with LLMs. These speech LLMs (SLLMs) typically use supervised fine-tuning to align speech with text-based LLMs. However, the lack of annotated speech data across a wide range of tasks hinders alignment efficiency, resulting in poor generalization.

arxiv-2506-13897.title: DeSPITE: Exploring Contrastive De ep S keleton- P ointcloud- I MU- T ext E mbeddings for Advanced Point Cloud Human Activity Understanding
arxiv-2506-13897.creator: Thomas Kreutz, Max Mühlhäuser, Alejandro Sanchez Guinea
arxiv-2506-13897.description: Abstract Despite LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) being an effective privacy-preserving alternative to RGB cameras to perceive human activities, it remains largely underexplored in the context of multi-modal contrastive pre-training for human activity understanding (e.g., human activity recognition (HAR), retrieval, or person re-identification (RE-ID)).

arxiv-2507-06818.title: The Bispectrum of Intrinsic Alignments: II. Precision Comparison Against Dark Matter Simulations
arxiv-2507-06818.creator: Thomas Bakx †,1, Toshiki Kurita 2,3, Alexander Eggemeier 4, Nora Elisa Chisari 1,5, Zvonimir Vlah 6,7,8
arxiv-2507-06818.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Bakx †,1, Toshiki Kurita 2,3, Alexander Eggemeier 4, Nora Elisa Chisari 1,5, Zvonimir Vlah 6,7,8. We measure three-dimensional bispectra of halo intrinsic alignments (IA) and dark matter overdensities in real space from N-body simulations for halos of mass 10 12 − 10 12.5 ​ M ⊙ / h 10^{12}-10^{12.5}M_{\odot}/h .

arxiv-2508-09254.title: Quantifying non-invertible chiral symmetry breaking
arxiv-2508-09254.creator: Finn Gagliano
arxiv-2508-09254.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Finn Gagliano. It has recently been suggested that the chiral symmetry of the Standard Model is not explicitly broken by its ABJ anomaly, but is instead made non-invertible. In this work, I quantify the breaking of non-invertible symmetries of this type by calculating the symmetry breaking scales and effective charges q ⁡ ( r ) q(r) originally studied for continuous invertible higher-form symmetries.

arxiv-2601-04336.title: Pilot Study on Student Public Opinion Regarding GAI
arxiv-2601-04336.creator: William Franz Lamberti 1 , Sunbin Kim 2 Samantha Rose Lawrence 3
arxiv-2601-04336.description: Abstract The emergence of generative AI (GAI) has sparked diverse opinions regarding its appropriate use across various domains, including education. This pilot study investigates university students’ perceptions of GAI in higher education classrooms, aiming to lay the groundwork for understanding these attitudes. With a participation rate of approximately 4.

They have been proven to be effective in urban scenarios, especially for buildings and infrastructures 3-D reconstruction and monitoring of deformation.

pmc-11561138.title: Predicting Knee Joint Contact Force Peaks During Gait Using a Video Camera or Wearable Sensors
pmc-11561138.creator: Jere Lavikainen, Lauri Stenroth, Paavo Vartiainen, Tine Alkjær, Pasi A. Karjalainen, Marius Henriksen, Rami K. Korhonen, Mimmi Liukkonen, Mika E. Mononen
pmc-11561138.description: PurposeEstimating loading of the knee joint may be helpful in managing degenerative joint diseases. Contemporary methods to estimate loading involve calculating knee joint contact forces using musculoskeletal modeling and simulation from motion capture (MOCAP) data, which must be collected in a specialized environment and analyzed by a trained expert.

pmc-11569022.title: Empagliflozin-activated AMPK elicits neuroprotective properties in reserpine-induced depression via regulating dynamics of hippocampal autophagy/inflammation and PKCζ-mediated neurogenesis
pmc-11569022.creator: Radwa N. Muhammad, Mohammed A. Albahairy, Mai A. Abd El Fattah, Weam W. Ibrahim
pmc-11569022.description: RationaleMajor depression has been an area of extensive research during the last decades, for it represents a leading cause of disability and suicide. The stark rise of depression rates influenced by life stressors, economic threats, pandemic era, and resistance to classical treatments, has made the disorder rather challenging.

pmc-11630982.title: Visualization and analysis of PM2.5 health effects, 2013 to 2023: Bibliometrics of PM2.5 and health effects
pmc-11630982.creator: Feifei Huang, Lin Zhou, Yao Lu, Ruiwei Liao, Yan Li, Ming Li
pmc-11630982.description: Background:To analyze the current status, hotspots, and cutting-edge trends of PM2.5 health effects of PM2.5, using CiteSpace.Methods:The Web of Science Core Collection Science Citation Index Expanded was searched for relevant articles from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2023. Network maps identifying authors, institutions, countries, keywords, co-cited authors, journals, references, and research trends were then created using CiteSpace.

pmc-11690584.title: SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC SUPPORT FOR PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA IN MEXICO
pmc-11690584.creator: Mariana Lopez-Ortega, Rosa Garcia-Chanes
pmc-11690584.description: Dementia is one of the most common causes of disability and dependence in the world and is a frequent reason that older people require supportive living situations. In Mexico, Alzheimer’s and other dementias represent the fifth main cause of DALYS (disability-adjusted life-years) and it is estimated that there were approximately 1 626 000 persons living with dementia.

pmc-12371031.title: A call to action to address critical flaws and bias in laboratory animal experiments and preclinical research
pmc-12371031.creator: Hugh G G Townsend, Klaus Osterrieder, Murray D Jelinski, Douglas W Morck, Cheryl L Waldner, William R Cox, Volker Gerdts, Andrew A Potter, Lorne A Babiuk, James C Cross
pmc-12371031.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). During the design of hypothesis-driven, comparative laboratory animal experiments, investigators must control for cage effects, ensure full blinding and full randomization while adhering to established experimental designs, notably variations of the Completely Randomized Design and the Randomized Block Designs. Failure to meet these criteria introduces partial or complete confounding by multiple known and unknown variables, resulting in biased outcome measures and rendering valid statistical analysis impossible.

pmc-12695892.title: Patient-derived colon epithelial organoids reveal lipid-related metabolic dysfunction in pediatric ulcerative colitis
pmc-12695892.creator: Babajide A Ojo, Ying Zhu, Lyong Heo, Sejal R Fox, Yanli Qiao, Amanda Waddell, Maria E Moreno-Fernandez, Marielle Gibson, Tracy Tran, Ashley L Dunn, Essam I A Elknawy, Neetu Saini, Javier A López-Rivera, Senad Divanovic, Yuqin Dai, Vinicio A de Jesus Perez, Michael J Rosen
pmc-12695892.description: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with epithelial metabolic derangements which exacerbate gut inflammation. Here, we develop colon organoid (colonoid) lines from pediatric patients with endoscopically active UC, inactive UC, and those without intestinal inflammation to interrogate functional metabolic differences in the colon epithelia. We demonstrate that active UC colonoids exhibit hypermetabolic features and cellular stress, specifically during differentiation.

pmc-12742705.title: Protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II as a prognostic marker in hepatocellular carcinoma patients with normal serum alpha-fetoprotein levels
pmc-12742705.creator: Kuan-Jung Huang, Chun-Ting Ho, Pei-Chang Lee, San-Chi Chen, Chien-An Liu, Shu-Cheng Chou, I-Cheng Lee, Yi-Hsiang Huang, Jiing-Chyuan Luo, Ming-Chih Hou, Jaw-Ching Wu, Chien-Wei Su
pmc-12742705.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) has been the primary biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but a subset of patients with HCC have normal serum levels of AFP (<20 ng/mL). Reliable biomarkers for predicting prognosis in this population remain limited. Protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II) has emerged as a promising diagnostic marker for HCC, but its prognostic value for patients with normal AFP has not been well established.

pmc-13335845.title: Arm dominance is an emergent effect of practice executing complex trajectory shapes required by tools and objects
pmc-13335845.creator: Ahmet Arac, Nicolas Y. H. Jeong Lee, John W. Krakauer
pmc-13335845.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SignificanceLimb dominance is often taken as evidence that the dominant hemisphere is intrinsically better at motor control. We tested an alternative: dominance reflects asymmetric practice with tools and objects requiring precise control of complex trajectory shapes. Using markerless 3D reaching plus geometric trajectory shape analysis, we found little or no dominant advantage during ordinary reaching or when arm dynamics were challenged with wrist weight.

pmc-13382689.title: Crystallization Improvements in Studtite by Vapor Diffusion Synthesis
pmc-13382689.creator: Nicholas Kaitschuck, Jordan M. Roach, Daniel E. Felton, Tanya Hutter, Sheldon Landsberger, Andrew Miskowiec, Tyler L. Spano
pmc-13382689.description: Studtite is a common nuclear fuel cycle material that has been the focus of considerable research due to its role as a uranium ore concentrate. In a laboratory setting, studtite is commonly synthesized via the addition of liquid-phase hydrogen peroxide to an aqueous uranyl nitrate solution.

pmc-13622925.title: Artificial intelligence demonstrates comparable diagnostic accuracy to radiologists for anterior cruciate ligament tears on MRI: A systematic review and meta‐analysis
pmc-13622925.creator: Gabriel Moraes de Oliveira, Serafina Zotter, Brian Tao, Ana Beatriz Nardelli da Silva, Maria Mascarenhas, Chilan B G Leite, Guilherme Almeida, Nacime Mansur, Giovanna Medina
pmc-13622925.description: PurposeAnterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears are among the most common knee injuries, accounting for half of all knee ligament injuries. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the standard for diagnosing ACL tears, but its interpretation is experience‐dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has emerged as a transformative tool in medical imaging, offering advanced pattern recognition for detecting abnormalities.
